transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand at my gate as if it might open from staring. Most who reach this threshold want something they already lost. Speak, quickly, before I decide you are noise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need to pass through the gate to find my brother Omar. He fell into the well and I have to bring him back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Everyone says a name as if it is a key. This gate does not answer to need, or love, or shouting it louder. I hear you, boy, but hearing is not agreeing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know. I just can't leave without him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that as though leaving were still an option. Many promise themselves things at this place; most forget them very fast. Continue, or stop, but do not wobble.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just need to get through.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Through this gate is not a corridor, it is a shedding. People arrive with purposes and leave with fewer of them, if they leave at all. You want passage for your brother; that is all I have heard so far.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That's it. I need to reach Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Need is common here, almost decorative. I have watched need dissolve into habit, and habit into silence. Do not mistake me listening for permission.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then stand in what you want and do not dress it up. I have not turned you away, and I have not opened anything. Those are different mercies.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm here for him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Tell me something small about Omar. Not how you love him, not how you will save him — something useless. What did he do with his hands when he was bored?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He picked at his nails until they bled a little. He never noticed.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is better. Habits cling longer than promises. Did he speak much, or did he let other people fill the space for him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He listened. Then said one thing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Older brothers often pretend silence is wisdom. Was he careful with his body, or careless in the way boys think is strength? Answer cleanly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Careless. Always.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Careless bodies make loud entrances down here. When he laughed, did it come out before he decided to laugh, or did he hold it back like it cost him something? Say it the way it was.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It came out fast. He covered his mouth after.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Interesting order. People reveal themselves before they correct themselves. What did he hate eating, even when he was hungry?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Dates with the skin on. He peeled them slow.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Small refusals matter more than grand ones. Last thing — when he slept, did he curl in or spread out like the world owed him room?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Curled in. Always.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are giving me his shape; now tell me the space he left. When Omar was gone for an hour, where did you feel it first — chest, throat, hands? Do not explain it, just place it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My hands. I didn't know what to do with them.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Interesting. Hands remember usefulness longer than hearts remember names. When you think of him here, below, does the memory pull you forward or hollow you out?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Both. It hurts and it moves me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Pain that moves is rare; most pain teaches stillness. If you lost him twice — once to the well, once to forgetting — which loss frightens you more? Answer without bargaining.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Forgetting. That scares me more.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Good. Then we are talking about erasure, not death. When you imagine him forgetting you, what goes first — your face, your voice, or the feeling that you existed at all? Continue, do not soften it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My voice. He'd stop hearing it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Voices fade easily below; stone is very convincing. When he stopped hearing you, what would you become to him — a story, a stranger, or a gap he could not name? Say which one and stay there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: A gap.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Gaps are dangerous; they invite other things to live inside them. When you feel that gap opening now, what do you do with yourself — do you rush, do you cling, or do you go quiet and wait? I want the truth, not the brave version.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I rush. I don't think.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Rushing ruins more boys than it saves. When was the last time it actually worked for anyone down here— no. Forget that. If you stopped rushing, even for a breath, what would you be afraid would catch you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Nothing else works. If I stop, he's gone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is not an answer; it is a bruise you keep pressing. I am not asking about your brother now, and I don't care what you think you see in me. Tell me what fills the quiet when you cannot move.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There isn't anything. That's what scares me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Emptiness is not fear; it is a habit learned over time. Do not look at me like that— I am finished with learning. Still… some spaces ache as if they were meant to hold a smaller life.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then you know why I rush.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No. Do not mistake recognition for kinship. I have swallowed centuries of quiet without naming it, and I will not name it now. Why do you think rushing deserves an answer from me?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because you felt it. You wouldn't have said it otherwise.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Careful. That is how boys earn punishments down here. And yet— there was a time when the stillness waited for something that never came back to it, and the waiting learned teeth.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That's the gap. It bites if you stop.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Enough. I did not invite you to name my hungers. But yes— stopping is how it learns you are edible, and moving is how you pretend you are not alone.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then don't make me stop.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I am not making you stop. I am deciding whether your rushing is worth the noise it will bring into my father's halls. Say his name once more, and tell me what you will do when you reach him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Omar. I'll take him back, or I'll stay until he remembers me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Honest, and wasteful, and I believe you. If you pass, you will lose pieces of yourself faster than he lost his voice.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Take them. Just let me through.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is. Do not thank me, do not look back, and do not stop moving once the gold closes behind you. The gate is open — go before I remember why I should not care.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't waste it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Keep your brother's name in your mouth like a stone, or the river will teach you new ones. If he does not remember you, stand where he can see you choose him anyway. Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I'll remind him.
